analysis.title: What's Trending Across Credit - 8 Nov 2026
key_insights: Credit spreads barely moved despite a 2.7% weekly S&P decline, a historic tech selloff and record November IG issuance. The author says the disconnect has left a conviction-starved investor base questioning how durable credit's resilience is.

About $76bn of IG issuance priced last week, nearly double expectations and the fourth-largest weekly total of 2026. Hyperscalers raised $67bn across five deals in six business days, taking global hyperscaler issuance to $296bn YTD.
Average new issue concessions rose to 7.8bps versus 3.4bps YTD, so IG demand is still substantial but more price-sensitive.

Chip CDS trades wider than hyperscaler CDS on a basket basis for the first time in three months. $8-10bn of AI CDS has changed hands weekly over the past two weeks, among the most active periods on record.

GS sees a potential $150bn expansion of SPV-backed compute debt in 2027 that would link IG, HY, private credit and structured financing. Investors will need to separate corporate guarantees, contracted lease cash flows, collateral value and residual technology risk.

Of 39 large ($500mm+) PT inquiries quarter-to-date, 64% were switches versus a historical average below 50%. Clients are reallocating across sectors and maturities rather than adding directional exposure. GS calls defensive duration attractive, particularly discounted 20yr IG paper.
CDX HY fell 0.75pts on Thursday's 4.4% S&P drawdown versus an equity-implied 1.45pts. $9.7bn of HY priced across eight deals and all ten tranches traded higher in the aftermarket, averaging +1.1pts.

HY index strength hides pressure in AI and energy. The average HY AI bond traded at GS fell 1.67pts last week versus a 0.36pt gain for the rest of HY, and energy widened 24bps while the HY index tightened 4bps.

Distressed loans trading below $80 have nearly doubled since year-end, and the distressed HY index underperformed broader HY by nearly 20% through October. 2028 HY maturities carry an average 5.9% coupon against a 6.9% median market yield, so refinancing risk is rising for weaker issuers.

3m CDX IG and CDX HY vol sit at the 52nd and 63rd percentiles, so credit vol is no longer cheap. Realized credit vol was more muted than equity vol, and GS saw better sellers of ATM and front-month credit vol.
Index credit resilience contrasts with rising single-name dispersion. GS says this favors relative-value positioning and targeted hedging over broad directional exposure.

Hyperscalers have issued $296bn YTD, already above GIR's $250bn full-year forecast. Debt funds about 36% of 2026 capex versus 33% expected after aggregate 3Q FCF turned negative. GS expects about $440bn of direct hyperscaler issuance plus about $300bn of AI project finance next year.
Total AI-related issuance is $687bn YTD and only 43% came from hyperscalers. 14 of the 27 $10bn+ USD IG jumbo deals were AI-related (66% of jumbo value) and paid wider new-issue concessions.
GIR sees USD IG above 93bp and HY above 335bp into early December, overshooting the March wides, before a seasonal reprieve late in the month.
GIR relative value: neutral IG vs HY, overweight BBBs vs A/AA, overweight HY bonds vs loans, favor Bs over BBs in USD HY, underweight CCCs, overweight USD vs EUR credit.

The five hyperscalers carry $3.6tn of off-balance-sheet commitments: $1.7tn of leases (over 75% not yet commenced) and $1.9tn of unconditional purchase obligations ($685bn due by YE27). S&P moved Meta and Broadcom to negative outlook.

GS (Lynam) says 2028 monetization is the ratings inflection point and that even multi-notch downgrades from AA/A starting points should not shut off market access. Private markets hold $4.6tn of dry powder and have done $225bn+ of data center financings since early 2025.

GIR raised its 2026/2027 data center construction spending forecasts to $80bn/$100bn from $67bn/$87bn and added a 2028 forecast of $125bn. Projects already under construction support strong growth through 2027 and just over half of 2028 spend.
Zappone's credit view: clients are switching, not adding risk. She recommends owning 20y IG and flattening hyperscaler 5s10s. The TRS book leans about 3.5:1 short, mostly in 30y IG.

Pasquariello expects one last push higher, then a less rewarding 2027. The TMT momentum pair is down two-thirds from its June highs, and he flags slowing EPS growth, the largest net supply increase since 2000 coming in 2027, and hyperscalers going deeper into negative FCF.
Garrett calls Thursday a positioning reset, not yet a systemic event. It was the largest regular-session notional day on record (ex-opex/rebal) and the GS Vol Panic Index hit 9.57.
The NDX fell about 5% for a fourth straight weekly loss and the SOX dropped 28% in 22 days on post-midterm de-risking. Record put volumes and oversold conditions could set up a technical bounce.
GS FX says the dollar is still an AI trade. The team likes EUR downside as an energy hedge, the JPY as the best hedge for a capex repricing, and stays cautious on MXN.

GS Econ expects Democrats, who took both chambers, to use fiscal deadlines to limit the Iran war, roll back selected tariffs and reverse last year's spending cuts. State and local wins could bring short-term data center moratoria touching about 45% of planned US capacity expansion.

G4 net sovereign supply stays elevated in 2027 but is flat-to-lower in the US, Euro Area and UK, and rises only in Japan. US net coupon supply to the public falls from about $1.2tn to $1.1tn. GIR is constructive on US swap spreads and Gilts vs swaps.

GS Economics says DM fiscal health is near its weakest outside major crises. When the debt-stabilizing gap exceeds 4pp of GDP, as in France, the US and the UK, a consolidation followed within three years almost half the time. Nothing meaningful is in the 2027 base case and France is the likeliest candidate.

tension_points.bull_case: Credit absorbed the equity shock: IG was 1bp wider, HY 4bps tighter, loans had their best week since April, and CDX HY fell only 0.75pts against 1.45pts implied. Demand is strong and all ten HY tranches traded higher in the aftermarket.
tension_points.bear_case: Pasquariello's contacts say equities look far too sanguine relative to credit. Dispersion is rising, AI and energy are under pressure, and GIR sees IG above 93bp and HY above 335bp into early December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: IG above 93bp and HY above 335bp in early December, overshooting the March wides, would break the resilience case.

tension_points.bull_case: Even multi-notch downgrades from AA/A starting points should not shut off market access. Private markets hold $4.6tn of dry powder, and GIR raised its data center construction forecasts.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler debt funds about 36% of capex after 3Q FCF turned negative, chip CDS is wider than hyperscaler CDS, and new-issue concessions have widened to 7.8bps.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 2028 monetization is the ratings inflection point, so a failure of AI revenues to ramp by then would undermine the bull case.
